Betacism.subject: World Geography
Betacism.question: The _____ was Sound change in historical linguistics.
Betacism.fact: In historical linguistics, betacism (UK: BEE-tə-siz-əm, US: BAY-) is a sound change in which [b] (the voiced bilabial plosive, as in bane) and [v] (the voiced labiodental fricative [v], as in vane) are confused. Betacism is a fairly common phenomenon; it has taken place in Greek, Hebrew, and several Romance languages.
